> **Status: Historical v1.x — inactive and unsupported.**

# Music Converter Voluntary Download Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Restore a voluntary download flow in the SpotMate browser scripts while keeping local launcher conversion disabled and hardening its HTTP boundary.

**Architecture:** script2.txt waits for the hidden inputs generated by the page after manual Turnstile verification, then converts sequentially only after an explicit click; script3.txt triggers HTTPS downloads only after a click, and script_complet.txt assembles this protocol into a standalone execution. server.js remains bound to 127.0.0.1, rejects non-local origins and hosts, bounds its inputs, and keeps POST /api/queue/start at 503.

**Tech Stack:** Node.js 18+ ESM, node:http server, node:child_process with execFile, node:test, vanilla browser JavaScript, CommonJS script tests, and npm with no new dependencies.

## Global Constraints

- The helper runs only on https://spotmate.online/en1 (or its canonical form with a trailing /) and never bypasses Turnstile/CAPTCHA.
- Hidden inputs must be those generated by the SpotMate DOM after manual verification; no synthetic track URL replaces a missing value.
- The dynamic CSRF token is read from the page at request time, stays local to the request closure, and is neither logged nor stored in window, the panel, or results.
- Conversions are sequential, limited to 100 tracks, and spaced 2000 ms apart; they start only after an explicit “Start conversions” click.
- Direct success accepts only a final HTTPS URL; task_id or taskId is polled at most 40 times every 4500 ms at /tasks/{id}.
- Errors 403, 419, 422, 429, and 500–599 are terminal with no automatic retry; network and schema errors are terminal with no automatic retry; every non-OK response ends the flow, and JSON is read only when Content-Type is `application/json`.
- “Cancel” stops polling, aborts the active request, and prevents the next track from starting.
- Downloads start only after an individual click or “Download all,” with 1500 ms between triggers; automatic hidden iframes are not allowed.
- CONVERSION_CAPABILITY.enabled remains false; POST /api/queue/start remains HTTP 503 and never calls queueManager.start.
- The server listens on 127.0.0.1; Host accepts only localhost:<port> or 127.0.0.1:<port> with the current port; each API POST requires a local same-origin Origin.
- Every response removes CORS *; incoming JSON must be application/json and is limited to 65536 bytes; /api/events accepts at most 8 SSE clients.
- Audio files are resolved and served only if they are real files confined under destinationDir; configuration is created and validated before assignment.
- Folder and browser launches use spawn or execFile with shell:false and separate arguments.
- Never add a real token, cookie, secret, or audio URL; assemble synthetic test values from fragments.
- Preserve the secret guard, inert diagnostics, old documents, and script1.txt unless there is strict evidence they must change.
- package.json moves from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0; CHANGELOG.md documents the compatible feature; the worker performs no tag, release, push, or PR.
- Work is sequential. No parallel worker: the three scripts and their tests share the same result protocol and timing limits.

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the minimum in server.js

Use the following contracts:

~~~js
function parseLocalHost(value, port) {
    const host = typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';
    const match = host.match(/^(localhost|127[.]0[.]0[.]1):([0-9]+)$/i);
    return Boolean(match && Number(match[2]) === port);
}

function parseLocalOrigin(value, port) {
    return value === 'http://localhost:' + port ||
        value === 'http://127.0.0.1:' + port;
}

function readJsonBody(req, maxBytes = 65536) {
    const contentType = String(req.headers['content-type'] || '').toLowerCase();
    if (!contentType.startsWith('application/json')) {
        return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('JSON content type is required.'), { statusCode: 415 }));
    }
    const declared = Number(req.headers['content-length'] || 0);
    if (declared > maxBytes) {
        req.resume();
        return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('JSON body is too large.'), { statusCode: 413 }));
    }
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const chunks = [];
        let size = 0;
        let settled = false;
        const settle = (error) => {
            if (settled) return;
            settled = true;
            req.resume();
            reject(error);
        };
        req.on('data', (chunk) => {
            size += Buffer.byteLength(chunk);
            if (size > maxBytes) {
                settle(Object.assign(new Error('JSON body is too large.'), { statusCode: 413 }));
                return;
            }
            chunks.push(chunk);
        });
        req.on('end', () => {
            if (settled) return;
            try {
                const parsed = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8') || '{}');
                settled = true;
                resolve(parsed);
            } catch (error) {
                settled = true;
                req.resume();
                reject(error instanceof Error ? Object.assign(error, { statusCode: 400 }) : Object.assign(new Error('Invalid JSON request body.'), { statusCode: 400 }));
            }
        });
        req.on('error', (error) => settle(Object.assign(error, { statusCode: 400 })));
    });
}

function isConfinedRegularFile(filePath, destinationDir) {
    const root = fs.realpathSync(destinationDir);
    const candidate = fs.realpathSync(filePath);
    const inside = candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root + path.sep);
    return inside && fs.statSync(candidate).isFile() ? candidate : null;
}
~~~

The handler checks Host against the server.address() port before any route,
checks Origin for every POST /api/*, rejects the ninth SSE client, and sets no
CORS header. For /api/queue/start, the
CONVERSION_CAPABILITY.enabled check remains before readJsonBody. Configuration builds
an absolute candidate, creates the directory, verifies it is a directory, then assigns
currentConfig in one operation. The audio route calls
isConfinedRegularFile before stat and createReadStream. Commands use
execCommand('explorer.exe', [dir], { shell: false }, cb); no command string is
constructed. The direct entry point reuses launchExecutable
with explorer.exe [url] on Windows, open [url] on macOS, and xdg-open [url] on
Linux, always with shell:false and separate arguments.

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the minimal helper in script2.txt

Implement this sequence in an IIFE without a global token:

~~~js
const MAX_TRACKS = 100;
const CONVERSION_GAP_MS = 2000;
const POLL_GAP_MS = 4500;
const MAX_POLLS = 40;

function finalHttpsUrl(value) {
    try { return new URL(value).protocol === 'https:' ? value : null; }
    catch { return null; }
}

function readPageCsrfToken() {
    const meta = document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]');
    if (meta) return meta.getAttribute('content') || meta.content || null;
    const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|; )XSRF-TOKEN=([^;]+)/);
    return match ? decodeURIComponent(match[1]) : null;
}

async function pollTask(taskId, signal) {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_POLLS; attempt += 1) {
        await sleep(POLL_GAP_MS, signal);
        const response = await fetch('/tasks/' + encodeURIComponent(taskId), {
            credentials: 'same-origin', signal
        });
        if (!response.ok) {
            return terminalError(response.status, 'HTTP error ' + response.status);
        }
        const responseContentType = String(response.headers.get('content-type') || '').toLowerCase();
        if (!responseContentType.startsWith('application/json')) {
            return terminalError(response.status, 'Invalid JSON response');
        }
        const payload = await response.json();
        if (payload?.error) {
            return terminalError(response.status, payload.message || 'Task error');
        }
        const info = payload?.data || {};
        const status = String(info.status || info.state || '').toLowerCase();
        const candidates = [
            info.url,
            info.download_url,
            info.data?.url,
            info.data?.download_url,
            info.result?.url,
            info.result?.download_url,
            payload.url,
            payload.download_url
        ];
        const url = candidates.map((candidate) => finalHttpsUrl(candidate)).find(Boolean);
        if (url) return { success: true, pending: false, url, error: null, status: response.status };
        if (['failed', 'error', 'expired', 'cancelled'].includes(status)) {
            return terminalError(response.status, info.message || payload.message);
        }
    }
    return terminalError('poll_timeout', 'Polling limit reached');
}

function terminalError(status, message) {
    return {
        success: false,
        pending: false,
        url: null,
        error: message || 'HTTP error ' + status,
        status
    };
}

function sleep(delayMs, signal) {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const timer = setTimeout(resolve, delayMs);
        signal.addEventListener('abort', () => {
            clearTimeout(timer);
            reject(new DOMException('Conversion cancelled.', 'AbortError'));
        }, { once: true });
    });
}

async function convertTrack(track, signal) {
    const csrfToken = readPageCsrfToken();
    const response = await fetch('/convert', {
        method: 'POST',
        credentials: 'same-origin',
        signal,
        headers: {
            accept: 'application/json',
            'content-type': 'application/json',
            ...(csrfToken ? { 'X-CSRF-TOKEN': csrfToken } : {})
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({ urls: track.value })
    });
    if ([403, 419, 422, 429].includes(response.status) || response.status >= 500) {
        return terminalError(response.status);
    }
    if (!response.ok) {
        return terminalError(response.status);
    }
    const responseContentType = String(response.headers.get('content-type') || '').toLowerCase();
    if (!responseContentType.startsWith('application/json')) {
        return terminalError(response.status, 'Invalid JSON response');
    }
    const data = await response.json();
    if (data?.error) {
        return terminalError(response.status, data.message || 'Task error');
    }
    const directUrl = finalHttpsUrl(data.url || data.download_url);
    if (directUrl) return { success: true, pending: false, url: directUrl, error: null, status: response.status };
    const taskId = (typeof data.task_id === 'string' && data.task_id.trim() ? data.task_id.trim() : null)
        || (typeof data.taskId === 'string' && data.taskId.trim() ? data.taskId.trim() : null);
    return taskId ? pollTask(taskId, signal) :
        terminalError(response.status, 'Final URL is missing or invalid');
}

async function convertSequentially(tracks, controller) {
    const results = [];
    for (let index = 0; index < tracks.length; index += 1) {
        if (controller.signal.aborted) break;
        const result = await convertTrack(tracks[index], controller.signal);
        results.push({ id: tracks[index].id, ...result });
        if (index < tracks.length - 1 && !controller.signal.aborted) {
            await sleep(CONVERSION_GAP_MS, controller.signal);
        }
    }
    window.fetchResults = results;
    return results;
}
~~~

collectTrackInputs reads only hidden inputs inside the
SpotMate container, deduplicates by name, requires a non-empty value, and throws an error above
100. waitForTrackInputs starts with a scan and then installs a
MutationObserver; the load action uses form.requestSubmit() on the
existing form after validating the entered URL. The panel installs
handlers without calling convertSequentially. The Start handler disables its
button, creates an AbortController, and starts the sequence; Cancel aborts it and updates the
visible state.

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the download panel

Filter with new URL(value).protocol === 'https:' and keep only
successful results, then create an anchor with a.href = url, target = '_blank',
and rel = 'noopener noreferrer' activated by the button handler. The download
trigger follows this pseudocode:

~~~js
function sleep(delayMs) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
}

function triggerUserDownload(url) {
    const link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = url;
    link.target = '_blank';
    link.rel = 'noopener noreferrer';
    link.click();
}

async function downloadAll(urls) {
    for (let index = 0; index < urls.length; index += 1) {
        if (index > 0) await sleep(1500);
        triggerUserDownload(urls[index]);
    }
}
~~~

Do not create an iframe or call triggerUserDownload during
installation, and do not log URLs. The global handler disables the
button during the loop and calls downloadAll after the user clicks.

- [ ] Step 1: Write the metadata RED test

~~~js
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');

test('1.1.0 metadata and changelog are consistent', () => {
    const metadata = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
    assert.deepEqual({
        name: metadata.name,
        version: metadata.version,
        private: metadata.private
    }, { name: 'music-converter', version: '1.1.0', private: true });
    const changelog = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'CHANGELOG.md'), 'utf8');
    assert(changelog.indexOf('## [Unreleased]') < changelog.indexOf('## [1.1.0] - 2026-08-25'));
    assert.match(changelog, /voluntary browser helper/);
});
~~~
